name: io.github.aniruddhaadak80/khata
description: A shared household ledger. Reads payment messages, records ledger lines, confirms or disputes them, and computes who pays whom in the fewest possible transfers. Every write is sealed into a per-line SHA-384 chain that can be replayed.

tools.name: get_khata_summary
tools.description: The current household, its members, its line count and the latest settlement.

tools.name: list_entries
tools.description: List ledger lines with filters for status, direction, category and member. Bounded at 100 rows.

tools.name: get_entry
tools.description: One ledger line plus its full seal chain.

tools.name: read_message
tools.description: Run the deterministic reader over messy payment text and return candidate ledger lines with per-field confidence and evidence.

tools.name: analyse_settlement
tools.description: Balances, a provably minimum-transfer plan, six weighted trust factors with their evidence, flags and a recommendation.

tools.name: record_entry
tools.description: Write one ledger line through the shared service layer. Converts at the live ECB rate, normalises the split and appends a sealed audit event. Supports idempotencyKey.

tools.name: record_entries
tools.description: Commit up to 50 reader candidates at once, reporting partial success honestly.

tools.name: decide_entry
tools.description: Confirm, dispute or edit a line. This is the step that changes who owes what, and it is sealed.

tools.name: delete_entry
tools.description: Soft-delete a line, keeping a tombstone so its seal chain stays replayable.

tools.name: export_statement
tools.description: Build the full settlement statement as JSON, with balances, transfers, factors, provenance and the seal.

tools.name: create_share_link
tools.description: Mint an unguessable link that renders a read-only statement anyone with the URL can open.

_notes.endpoint: The URL in `packages[0].transport.url` is the live production alias. A preview deployment serves the same endpoint at its own origin.
_notes.handshake: POST a JSON-RPC 2.0 `initialize`, then `notifications/initialized`, then `tools/list`. Call tools with `tools/call`.
_notes.scoping: There are no accounts. Every call is scoped to the anonymous HTTP-only cookie session that first opened the site, so an agent must act inside the same browser session as the person whose ledger it is reading.
